stories.headline: Jack Smith defends Trump probes as GOP senators grill him for four hours
stories.summary: Former special counsel Jack Smith spent roughly four hours before the Senate Judiciary Committee defending his two Trump prosecutions while Republican senators accused him of partisanship and mapping the GOP apparatus. Chairman Chuck Grassley said Smith took partisanship to a new level and vowed to keep investigating; Smith insisted the strongest witnesses in the 2020 election case would have been Republicans and that he will not be silenced by threats of prosecution. Tempers flared when Sen. Eric Schmitt briefly accused Smith of attending an Atlanta Hawks game around the Fani Willis scandal, only for colleagues to note Smith had attended an Iowa Hawkeyes women's basketball game featuring Caitlin Clark.

stories.headline: CBP put $20 million behind Trump-heavy TV ads ahead of midterms, CNBC reports
stories.summary: U.S. Customs and Border Protection funded the taxpayer-backed television spots featuring President Trump that have drawn bipartisan scrutiny weeks before the November midterms, CNBC reported, citing a Wall Street Journal account. Top Democrats say Homeland Security dedicated about $20 million to the effort, including money routed through Republicans' One Big Beautiful Bill Act, and federal records show a $20 million CBP award to Maryland ad firm LMD Agency days earlier. The White House called the spots patriotic public service announcements; watchdog groups asked FCC, FTC, GAO, and the Office of Special Counsel to examine alleged propaganda and Hatch Act issues.

stories.headline: Video: workers scramble as ICE raids Tallahassee food truck
stories.summary: Security footage from Chile & Chili's Taqueria in Tallahassee shows food-truck workers scrambling as Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents rolled up Friday, with one woman detained on camera. The owner told local station WCTV that three Guatemalan nationals in the video had not finished immigration paperwork, and he later closed the truck after remaining staff quit amid safety concerns. Community organizers planned an anti-ICE rally at the Tennessee Street location for Wednesday while a related GoFundMe raised nearly $13,000.

stories.headline: Candace Owens hit with second defamation suit over Charlie Kirk murder theories
stories.summary: Washington State native Robert Hild, a private citizen who was in the crowd when Charlie Kirk was assassinated at Utah Valley University, sued podcaster Candace Owens on Monday for suggesting he helped kill Kirk. The 73-page federal complaint says Owens told millions of listeners that Hild resembled FBI suspect photos, had ties to foreign actors, and belonged to a gothic communist underground, triggering threats, doxxing, and vandalism. Owens already faces an April defamation suit from Kirk's former private security chief over similar alternate theories that reject the case against suspected assassin Tyler Robinson.

stories.headline: Trumbull football drops to 1–2 after 28–21 home loss to Norwalk
stories.summary: Trumbull High's football Eagles fell 28–21 to Norwalk on Friday after a 14–14 halftime tie, dropping to 1–2 and extending a six-game home losing streak dating to last season. Brayden Jagoe rushed for 182 yards and two touchdowns for Trumbull, but Norwalk's Easton Pace ran for 271 yards and four scores. The Eagles host Shelton at 7:00 p.m. Friday; a full game replay is on the NFHS Network.

stories.headline: Tesla locks in $30 billion in credit lines to scale Cybercab, Optimus, and Semi
stories.summary: Tesla announced Tuesday that Citibank agreed to a $20 billion three-year delayed-draw term loan, with Wells Fargo adding an $8 billion five-year revolver and a $2 billion 364-day facility — $30 billion in fresh credit capacity aimed at scaling Cybercab, Optimus, and the Semi. The company said it does not plan to draw on the facilities this year even as it projects at least $25 billion in 2026 capital spending, finishing Q2 with roughly $9 billion in debt and more than $40 billion in cash and investments. All three products require new manufacturing lines, including dedicated factories for Semi and Optimus.

stories.headline: Penguins unveil 60th-anniversary logo, giveaways, and Oct. 3 home-opener ceremony
stories.summary: The Pittsburgh Penguins will mark their 60th anniversary all season with special events, ticket packages, and giveaways, starting with a pregame ceremony at the Oct. 3 home opener against Montreal. A retro-inspired anniversary logo with five Stanley Cup stars and three-river stripes will appear on helmets all year and on jersey shoulders for that opener. Planned giveaways include lapel pins, a kitchen apron, a poster, and a patterned shirt, plus era-night T-shirts and a limited Zamboni gravy boat for select packages.

stories.headline: Jets film room: Geno Smith’s 13.1% explosive-play rate nearly sparked a Lions comeback
stories.summary: Official Jets film breakdown credits Geno Smith with seven explosive passing plays and a 13.1% explosive-play rate — ninth-best in the NFL in Week 3 — in the 31–24 loss at Detroit. Smith was 31-of-37 for 321 yards and three touchdowns with no interceptions, hitting Kenyon Sadiq and Garrett Wilson for explosive scores and posting a 146.8 rating on deep balls this season. Coach Aaron Glenn said the late push showed belief the team can win any game; next up is Chicago's 13th-ranked pass defense at Soldier Field.

stories.headline: Apple CEO Ternus pushes faster year-round launches and a leaner engineering org
stories.summary: According to Bloomberg's Mark Gurman, Apple CEO John Ternus wants the company to broaden its device lineup, lean harder on engineering, and loosen the traditional spring/fall release cadence so new products can ship more often through the year. Plans discussed include fewer middle managers, hiring restraint, reduced marketing spend, and more experimental bets for the AI era, with directors and engineering program managers already given weeks to find internal roles or face layoff. Gurman cautions the cultural shift could take years even as product groups feel pressure to deliver more on shorter timelines.

stories.headline: Apple Creator Studio and Final Cut Camera add iPhone 18 Pro aperture tools
stories.summary: Apple updated Creator Studio apps and Final Cut Camera to tap the iPhone 18 Pro's variable aperture, with aperture- and shutter-priority modes, cinematic effects, false-color overlays, improved focus peaking, and a tally light for recording. Pages, Numbers, and Keynote gained templates and collaboration tools; Pixelmator Pro on iPad picked up Select and Mask; Freeform added Dark Mode, folders, and Writing Tools for handwritten notes. Creator Studio remains $12.99 a month for the full creative suite, with some Freeform and iWork extras bundled as premium features.

stories.headline: NHTSA closes Jeep Wrangler/Gladiator underhood-fire probe after 1.08M-vehicle recall
stories.summary: Federal safety regulators closed Preliminary Evaluation PE24024 into underhood fires on Jeep Wrangler JL and Gladiator JT trucks after FCA's June recall of nearly 1.08 million 2021–2025 vehicles. Investigators tied the risk to a high-resistance electrical connection at the electric-hydraulic power steering pump that can overheat and ignite nearby materials, sometimes while the vehicle is parked. NHTSA said the recall addresses the defect it was investigating and will keep monitoring the field; unrepaired owners are still advised to park outside and away from buildings.

stories.headline: Fall color wave is rolling south — peak windows still run about one week
stories.summary: America's 2026 fall foliage season is already moving from high country and northern states toward lower elevations and the South, with most destinations near historical peak averages. Planners note peak color at any single spot usually lasts about a week, so timing a Vermont Northeast Kingdom drive versus a Great Smoky Mountains foothills trip can differ by weeks. The piece walks west-to-east and north-to-south windows — Colorado aspens, New England late September openers, Mid-Atlantic mid-October, and Southern Appalachians lasting into November — and urges checking local reports in the final week before travel.

stories.headline: Gun-rights groups sue Jacksonville over venue bans that turned carriers away at EverBank Stadium
stories.summary: Florida Carry Inc. and Gun Owners of America, joined by individual plaintiffs, sued the City of Jacksonville, Mayor Donna Deegan, and Sheriff T.K. Waters over written and unwritten policies that allegedly forced legally armed visitors to disarm, denied them entry, or threatened trespass at EverBank Stadium, the Florida Theatre, and the performing-arts center. The complaint leans on Florida's firearm-preemption statute, which reaches local policies and directives and allows injunctions, fees, and capped damages. The filing follows Attorney General James Uthmeier's separate May suit over City Hall firearm logbooks; the city said it was served and directed questions to counsel.
